content: Your days are numbered. Use them to throw open the windows of your soul to the sun. If you do not, the sun will set, and you with it.
author: Marcus Aurelius
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. Reminding yourself of your mortality is not morbid; it is the most clarifying lens available to human consciousness. When you remember that your days are strictly numbered, petty resentments and trivial anxieties evaporate.

In Marcus Aurelius's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Death gives urgency and sweetness to every ordinary afternoon. Because this day will never come again, the way you spend your attention right now is of monumental significance.
reflectionPrompt: Where in your current routine are you choosing convenient illusion over uncomfortable truth?
